newsitem.title: USA: Fed presidents watchful of new banking technology.
newsitem.headline: Fed presidents watchful of new banking technology.

text.p: Four Federal Reserve bank presidents debated on Friday how modern technology affects the U.S. banking industry and the role of the central bank.

The four Fed presidents -- Thomas Hoenig of Kansas City, Jerry Jordan of Cleveland, Thomas Melzer of St. Louis and Michael Moskow of Chicago -- were hosts at a symposium organized by the University of St. Louis-Missouri.
St. Louis Fed President Thomas Melzer emphasized confidence in the U.S. monetary authority and the payments system is key to long-term growth.

"For our nation to achieve maximum sustainable growth, users of the payments system must have confidence in the monetary authority," said Melzer, who stressed that new forms of payments, such as electronic currency, must ultimately be transformed into money.
"Changes in the purchasing power of money, that is the inflation rate, will continue to be influenced by the Federal Reserve's control over the supply of base money."
Moskow emphasized the need for the U.S. central bank to remain a federal institution with regional banks.
"Our regional system facilitates the development of effective, long-term policy. It provides insulation from day-to-day political pressures," Moskow noted.
Kansas City's Hoenig elaborated on the theme, "How is the central bank's mission to supervise financial intermediaries going to be fulfilled?"
Cleveland's Jordan discussed "What are the implications of innovations in communications technologies for commercial banks?"
Several pieces of legislation are pending in Congress about the mandate and shape of the Fed System.
The bank presidents declined to discuss the economy or monetary policy ahead of the early February meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.
